questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be used if you share the lane with another vehicle.
Usually gives good traction, except when it is raining.
Should never be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives good traction, except when it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip of the road can be oily, but it usually provides enough grip for safe riding, except in rain. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide. Riders can ride on either side of the strip and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a way to stay in control during a motorcycle turn?

options.text: Speed up while turning.
Slow down before you turn.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up while turning.
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before entering the turn. Look in the direction you want to go. Press on the handlebar to lean the right way. Then roll on the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Move slowly toward the dog, then speed up fast as it gets close.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly toward the dog, then speed up fast as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If you see a dog coming toward you, slow down and downshift until you are near it. Then quickly speed up and away as the dog gets close.

questions.question: One of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to have your headlight on all the time. Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: A sign your front tire is flat is when steering suddenly feels:

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake.
Both brakes are equally strong.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake on a motorcycle is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually, that means the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: When you cannot see into an intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal and then go normally.
Flash your lights and honk to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a place where you cannot see into the intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection with no signs or lights at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
questions.explanation: If you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time as another driver, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When riding with other motorcyclists, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should be used at all times.
Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway.
Should be used when riding around curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually good, but switch to single-file when turning, riding in curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, how should the following distance change?

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The trailer adds weight, so the motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What causes an engine to seize?

options.text: A lack of oil.
A lack of fuel.
Improper tire inflation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lack of oil.
questions.explanation: An engine seizes when it does not have enough oil. Without oil, engine parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it.
Release the front brake immediately and only use the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the brake right away and then re-apply it.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes when approaching an intersection. This reduces your reaction time if you need to stop.

questions.question: What color and design are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When turning, how should you look through the turn?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look where you want to go through the turn. Turn only your head and keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders can cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front so you can use its lights.
Keep riding at your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. You cannot see as well at night and need more time and space to react to dangers.

questions.question: When being passed, should you move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: Yes, because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
No, because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
It does not matter because it has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may signal the passing driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-fourths of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: In broad daylight.
At dusk.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: In broad daylight.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Constantly look in the rearview mirror.
Check your rearview mirror often.
Not use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirror often while riding. Always use your mirror before changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is in the left part of a lane, next to the centerline.
Is in the right part of a lane, next to the curb.
Changes based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best lane position depends on the situation. Choose a position that gives you the best visibility and space around you. Move your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can be operated:

options.text: Only during the day.
Without a driver license.
With any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: With any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any type of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.
